newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Sasol to post bumper year profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sasol to post bumper year profit.

text.p: South African synthetic fuels producer Sasol Ltd is set to post a jump in year profits on Monday boosted by a weak rand and strong product prices, analysts said on Friday.
"They will be a pretty healthy set of results. They have really had a year when everything has gone right for them," one analyst said.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast a pre-exceptional earnings per share figure in a range of 385-400 cents with a consensus figure of 390 cents against 323 last time. The dividend is seen being hiked to 120 cents a share from 102 last year.

Sasol, which produces fuels from coal and also has a large chemicals operation, benefits from a weak rand against the dollar. This is because its costs are mostly rand-based and its prices largely U.S. dollar-based.

Analysts said the weakness of the rand, which has lost a quarter of its value against the dollar since the middle of February, would reap rewards for the group although they pointed out Sasol operated with a relatively strong rand for more than half the financial year.
"The main benefit from the currency weakness is going to come through into 1997," said Mark Ingham, oils analyst at Frankel Pollak.

Even without benefits from the international currency markets Sasol has impressed the market, analysts said. The firm has enjoyed a good pricing environment for its products, such as petrol and diesel. "It's a mixture of currency and product prices," one analyst said.
The group's chemical operations have also performed well with the division seen making big inroads into traditional markets and netting high profits.
The firm's tariff protection for its fuels side is being phased out and the firm has put much of its energy into growing its chemicals businesses.
"The chemicals operations are really starting to come through," one analyst said.
